paras: The Jeanerette acid-attack manhunt was a posse search in Jeanerette, Louisiana, on October 29, 1903, for an unidentified man believed to be Black who had thrown sulphuric acid in the face of an engineer, Norther Provost. Two Black men were arrested and released, the assailant was not caught, and the dispatch reported that he would be "summarily dealt with" if captured.

Provost was an engineer employed by Jos. A. Provost and lived in Jeanerette. According to the St. Martinville Weekly Messenger, several murders had recently been committed in the town and many Black residents had been "ordered to leave the town."

At about 6 a.m., as Provost opened his door to go to work, a man threw a large quantity of sulphuric acid in his face and escaped; Provost believed the man was "a negro," and it was reported that he might lose his eyesight. Once he gave the alarm, a posse of citizens and officers set out after the assailant, and Capt. J. L. Row of Hope Plantation, summoned by telephone, brought his hounds. The dogs could not follow the trail because many people had been on the premises before they arrived.

Two Black men were arrested and brought before Mrs. L. A. Moresi, a neighbor who had seen a Black man run from Provost's yard at the time of the assault. When she failed to identify them, they were released.

The dispatch described "much excitement" and citizens "thoroughly aroused," and said the guilty person would be "summarily dealt with" if captured. No report of a capture, trial or lynching appears in the coverage.

The New Iberia Enterprise and Independent Observer printed the Jeanerette dispatch on October 31, giving the assailant's race only as Provost's belief. A week later the Weekly Messenger reprinted the same text, spelling the name "Northern Provost," under a preface declaring that "Jeanerette is infested with a class of worthless negroes" and that the attack showed not all of the "worthless darkies" ordered out had left. No Black-press coverage of the attack or the manhunt was found.

reader.title: Jeanerette acid-attack manhunt
bases: A posse of citizens and officers hunted with hounds for an unidentified man believed to be Black, two Black men were arrested and released, and the dispatch said the guilty man would be 'summarily dealt with' if caught; no one was reported injured or killed by the posse (A3, A5).
All facts come from one Jeanerette dispatch (A3); the Weekly Messenger item (A5) reprints the same text with an editorial preface, so it is not an independent report.

accounts.label: Jeanerette dispatch
accounts.gist: An unknown man believed by Provost to be Black threw acid in his face; a posse with hounds failed to track him, two Black men were arrested and released, and the dispatch predicted summary punishment if the guilty man was caught.

accounts.label: Weekly Messenger editorial preface
accounts.gist: Presented the attack as proof that not all of Jeanerette's 'worthless darkies' had obeyed orders to leave town after recent murders.

framing.detail: The New Iberia paper ran the dispatch without a headline of its own in the text, reporting the assailant's race only as Provost's belief and the threatened 'summarily dealt with' without comment.
The Weekly Messenger framed the attack with 'Jeanerette is infested with a class of worthless negroes' and endorsed the earlier orders for Black residents to leave town.

conflicts.note: Same dispatch text; the New Iberia printing is the earlier and closer one.

record_check.dossier: Provost was the victim of the acid attack; the targets of the posse were the unidentified assailant believed to be Black and two unnamed Black men who were arrested and released.
Black: the assailant was 'believed' to be 'a negro' and the two men arrested were 'negroes'; Provost's race is not stated.
pursuit with hounds, arrest (two men, released), threat

info: About 6 a.m., October 29, 1903 (dispatch dateline 'this morning'; Weekly Messenger: 'Thursday of last week')
Targets of the pursuit: the unidentified assailant, believed Black (at large), and two unnamed Black men arrested and released; Norther Provost was the victim of the acid attack, not of the posse

An unknown man, whom Provost believed was a 'negro', threw a large quantity of sulphuric acid in the face of engineer Norther Provost as he opened his door to go to work; Provost might lose his eyesight
A posse of citizens and officers, with Capt. J. L. Row of Hope Plantation and his hounds
The assailant escaped; no report of a capture, trial or lynching was found
